Looking for a complete game that is feature complete and free of the worst bugs? Then buy this later!

Looking to support a game studio with a fresh take on co-op with a mix of Vermintide and Minecraft that is entertaining now and might be super great later? Then buy this now!

I can see a lot of potential here and its good fun with friends.  Don't expect a completed upgrade tree and vanity items store. Check the Experimental branch.  If they add even a smidge of crafting to this game, it'll be a Space Dwarf's dream.

Rough around the edges, but shows considerable promise. The premises of the core gameplay loop (your moment to moment actions) and secondary gameplay loop (what you do during the course of a game) are sturdy enough that I can see this game standing the test of time. Game mechanics encourage teamwork and make going alone dangerous by forcing the players to need each other. The caves are generally unpredictable, maps can be changed through tunneling and explosives and boss enemies trying to dig to you, and combined with random enemy waves the game design adds considerable replay value.

The game play is a blend of Left 4 Dead and Minecraft, where you drop into a cave system, need to gather minerals and/or deal with the wildlife infestation, and at the end of the mission you have to make a dash for the escape while the local fauna attempt to eat you while you drill, blast, zipline, and platform your way out. The progression system is not mandatory or overbearing, as it is quite possible to beat the hardest settings with a fresh character if you coordinate with your team. The enemies have weak points that reward aiming and coordinating with teammates to flank.

The devs also seem to be dedicated to qualify of life updates, which quite honestly I wish I saw more of. They have so far avoided the majority of the gameplay elements that turn coop games unpleasant, such as that green circle in Vermintide 2 that made it into a kill competition, or the fire panic mechanics in Killing Floor 2 that allowed bad or trolling firebugs to make it impossible for his teammates to land headshots. The P2P network seems surprisingly robust.

This game has also managed to avoid many of the problems that turn many early access, co-op, and/or procedurally generated games into garbage. The devs communicate and are active in the fan communities. They added more lobby management systems, and seem to genuinely recognize some of the realities that come with managing of a team of randoms in a game that demands coop. While the caves are procedurally generated, this is done to maintain freshness as opposed to as excuse to put 0 effort in environment design, as much of the cave design draws from pre-sets so as to prevent extremely convoluted or unnavigatable caves. While there are certainly some balance issues, they are steadily being ironed out.

Overally, I would strong recommend that if you're interested in coop games to give DRG a chance.

I got this game on a whim after seeing some gameplay and deciding to give it a go. After all, space dwarves.

So far it has proven to be a very entertaining and engaging game. It can get a little repetative if played for extended periods of time but if played in small amounts it can provide a great deal of amusement. With the very active development team there is a lot of promise at the moment for future updates and additional content to enhance the game.

Overall it is a fairly simple premise, you're a dwarf and you're digging a hole. What's in that hole is the critical part with missions ranging from simple mining operations to retrieval missions and even search and destroy. The entire affair takes place with a team of four dwarves of any of four classes which each bring their own unique talents and abilities to the table. Learning how best to utilize the various unique talents of each class is part of the fun and the constant encroachig darkness of the caves you explore add a sense of tension to everything.

It doesn't help that there are some very nasty critters out there waiting for you.

Perhaps the best thing about this game is that the community is incredibly positive. I've only had two negative interactions within the game in the few weeks I've been playing. Everything else has been quite positive and even humorous at times.

If you're looking for a new cooperative game to pass the time and have some fun in then I would say this is the game for you. Give it a spin, you can never dig too deep.
A fun game to play friends that gets better with each update.
Great game; the community needs to get the word out so more people can discover what makes this game special. Keep the positive reviews coming and let people know about DRG!
